hook.line: English lets you say "I haven't the faintest idea" or "Never in my life." Spanish has the same tools, and they all lean on a *no* (or a fronted *en mi vida*) to work.

examples.es: En mi vida había visto algo así.
examples.en: Never in my life had I seen anything like it.

examples.es: No hizo el más mínimo esfuerzo.
examples.en: He didn't make the slightest effort.

examples.es: No tengo ni la más remota idea.
A Hernando no le hizo la menor gracia.
examples.en: Hernando didn't find it the least bit funny.

rule: Words like *la menor idea*, *gran cosa* and *el más mínimo esfuerzo* only work in a negative sentence, so *no* comes first: *No tengo la menor idea*. Without it, the sentence says nothing sensible. Another way to get "never": start with *en mi vida* and drop the *no*: *En mi vida había visto algo así*. If *en mi vida* comes at the end, bring the *no* back: *No he visto algo así en mi vida*. Note *No es gran cosa*: no *una*.
smallPrint: Teachers call these negative polarity items: expressions that need a negative around them.

options: I haven't the faintest idea.
I have a good idea.
I had an idea.
It's a big deal.
It's no big deal.
It's a great thing.

readAndPick.es: En mi vida había visto algo así.
options: I've seen this a lot in my life.
I saw something like it once.
Never in my life had I seen anything like it.

readAndPick.es: No hizo el más mínimo esfuerzo.
options: He made the slightest effort.
He didn't make the slightest effort.
He made a big effort.

readAndPick.es: No tengo ni la más remota idea.
options: I haven't the remotest idea.
I have the remotest idea.
I had a remote idea.

readAndPick.es: A Hernando no le hizo la menor gracia.
options: Hernando found it very funny.
Hernando found it a little funny.
Hernando didn't find it the least bit funny.

readAndPick.es: No he visto algo así en mi vida.
options: I've seen something like it all my life.
I haven't seen anything like it in my life.
I'll see something like it in my life.

readAndPick.es: No tengo la menor idea de qué pasa.
options: I haven't the faintest idea what's going on.
I know exactly what's going on.
I had no idea what went on.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *No tengo* or *Tengo* and type the whole sentence: *___ la menor idea.*
yourTurn.why: *La menor idea* only works with a *no* in front.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: It's no big deal.
Type in Spanish: Never in my life had I seen anything like it.
yourTurn.answer: En mi vida había visto algo así.
accept: No había visto algo así en mi vida.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: He didn't make the slightest effort.
yourTurn.answer: No hizo el más mínimo esfuerzo.
yourTurn.why: *No* plus *el más mínimo* gives "not the slightest".

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative, with the end phrase. Say: I haven't seen anything like it in my life.
yourTurn.answer: No he visto algo así en mi vida.
accept: No había visto algo así en mi vida.
yourTurn.why: *En mi vida* at the end needs the *no* back at the verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Hernando didn't find it the least bit funny.
yourTurn.answer: A Hernando no le hizo la menor gracia.
yourTurn.why: *No* comes before *le hizo*, then *la menor gracia*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I haven't the faintest idea what's going on.
yourTurn.answer: No tengo la menor idea de qué pasa.
yourTurn.why: *De qué pasa* adds what you have no idea about.

pitfalls.why: Almost. *La menor idea* needs a *no* to make the negative.
Almost. In this fixed phrase there is no *una*.

pitfalls.wrong: He visto algo así en mi vida.
pitfalls.right: No he visto algo así en mi vida.
pitfalls.why: Almost. Without *no* at the verb, it says you have seen it.

personal: Say something you haven't the faintest idea about, starting with *No tengo la menor idea de*.
